papers.title: SENTRY: A Streaming Edge Network Trust Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Real-time voice cloning has enabled large-scale streaming deepfake and vishing attacks, while existing Network Detection and Response (NDR) solutions rely on GPU-based post-processing that requires buffered audio and generalizes poorly to unseen speech synthesis models. This paper presents SENTRY, a hardware-oriented, streaming trust engine for inline deepfake detection at the network edge. SENTRY employs an integer lifting-wavelet front end together with a bank of multiplier-free transforms, including wavelet-packet envelopes, Walsh-Hadamard sequency profiles, waveform micro-statistics, and long-term spectral features, designed so that acoustic analysis needs only integer add, shift, compare and bitwise operations. A supervised gradient-boosted tree classifier is combined with an unsupervised Mahalanobis out-of-distribution detector trained solely on authentic speech, and their outputs are fused by a lightweight logistic layer to produce graduated LOG, CHALLENGE, or DROP actions. Under a closed-set protocol, SENTRY reaches 98.75% accuracy at a 1.25% equal-error rate (EER) on WaveFake, with perfect separation of HiFi-GAN and WaveGlow; its supervised track alone achieves an AUC of 0.9994 (fused: 0.9993). On ASVspoof 2019 LA (attacks A01-A06) over an 8 kHz mu-law telephony channel, it reaches 94.75% accuracy at a 5.05% EER, with a supervised-track AUC of 0.9948 (fused: 0.9884) and per-attack EERs below 7%. In our prototype, the feature front end runs as bit-exact integer code on one Arm Cortex-A53 core, and the classifier and fusion stage are synthesized for a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC using no DSP slices, returning a decision 220 ns after a feature vector is ready. These results indicate that deepfake screening can be placed inline without GPUs or floating-point hardware; generalization to unseen generators is left to future work.

papers.title: Long Listening Thoughts: Eliciting Open Auditory Reasoning with Deliberative Perception and Cognitive Refinement
papers.abstract: We introduce Long Listening Thoughts (LLT), a framework for constructing post-training datasets that improves audio reasoning by pairing deliberate perceptual grounding with explicit cognitive behaviors. On audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks, large audio-language models (LALMs) are limited primarily by perceptual errors, yet existing post-training datasets rely on audio descriptions of limited diversity. Through a four-stage pipeline, LLT (1) builds multi-aspect dense audio descriptions spanning semantic, acoustic, and temporal information, (2) generates more challenging questions, (3) synthesizes incorrect reasoning traces, and (4) extends short reasoning traces into long ones via a thought-continuation strategy that elicits cognitive behaviors such as verification and backtracking. Using LLT, we synthesize 1.6M reasoning traces and train Qwen2.5-Omni-7B with a two-stage pipeline of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by direct preference optimization (DPO). This improves accuracy on MMAU Test-mini (71.5 to 78.2), MMAR (56.7 to 63.7), and MMSU (60.6 to 66.0).

## Model Description

**Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0** is an audio-capable version of [Luciole-8B-Instruct-1.1](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Instruct-1.1).
The model was developed by [LINAGORA](https://linagora.com) and
the [OpenLLM-France](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France) consortium, as part of the OpenLLM France project funded by
[BPI France](https://www.bpifrance.fr/) under the France 2030 program.

The training of Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0 was conducted on the Jean Zay supercomputer managed by [IDRIS](http://www.idris.fr/docs/idris/missions),
using the [NVIDIA NeMo Speech](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech) toolkit.
The model was trained on various tasks and types of audio, including ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition), AST (Automatic Speech Translation), QA (Question Answering), Sound (Question Answering and Captioning), Music (Question Answering and Captioning) and more.

### Bias, Risks, and Limitations

- Inherits the limitations of the base [Luciole-8B-Instruct-1.1](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Instruct-1.1)
  language model: it can struggle with math word problems and is susceptible to hallucination.
- Training sequences were capped at 16,384 tokens (audio and text combined), so longer contexts are untested.
<!-- - The audio encoder and its front-end were entirely frozen during training, so audio understanding is bounded by what
  Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 already hears: the model cannot learn to compensate for acoustic conditions the
  encoder itself handles poorly. -->
- Language coverage is uneven. French and English make up most of the training mix and are the only languages seen on every task. German, Spanish and Italian were seen in training for ASR, AST and spoken QA. Portuguese, Dutch and Arabic for ASR and AST only.
- Arabic is the weakest language: the frozen Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 encoder was not trained on Arabic,
  so the model is clearly less reliable there (FLEURS WER ~30%).
<!-- - LoRA fine-tuning only touches attention projections in the LLM; no additional audio-specific safety or
  refusal tuning was performed beyond what the base LLM already has. -->

### Recommendations

- Speech, sound and music understanding (summarization, captioning, sound/music QA, conversation):
  best in French and English, the only languages the model was trained on for these tasks.
- Transcription (ASR) and translation (AST): supported in French, English, German, Spanish,
  Italian, Portuguese and Dutch. For production ASR/AST pipelines, a dedicated model may still
  perform better.
- Spoken question answering: mainly supported in French and English. German, Spanish and
  Italian are also supported, but with far less training data.
- Other languages and tasks: outside French and English, evaluate the model on your own data
  before relying on it, especially for a task the model was not trained on in that language.
- Up-to-date or domain-specific knowledge: as with the base LLM, pair the model with a RAG
  pipeline.

## Training details

### Training data

Trained on the [OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training-Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training-Dataset),
a large multilingual, multi-task collection of audio–text conversations comprising: ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition),
AST (Automatic Speech Translation), spoken question answering, summarization, diarization, temporal localization,
speaker/gender/age/emotion/language recognition, and music/sound captioning and QA (Question Answering).

### Instruction template

Same chat template as the base LLM (inspired by Qwen3), extended with an `<|audio|>` locator tag:
wherever `<|audio|>` appears in a turn, the corresponding audio segment is encoded and its embeddings
replace the tag before the sequence reaches the LLM. Conversations can carry several audio clips and mix
audio-only, text-only, and audio+text turns within the same dialogue (see the
[dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training-Dataset) for example
conversations).

### Training Procedure

| Component | Details |
|---|---|
| **Audio encoder** | [Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3) Conformer encoder, frozen |
| **RoTE** | Applied between audio encoder and audio adapter. θ=1200, rotary fraction=0.2. Inspired by [Goel et al., 2024, OMCAT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12109).|
| **Audio adapter** | Linear projection into the LLM embedding space (1024 -> 4096) |
| **LLM** | [Luciole-8B-Instruct-1.1](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Instruct-1.1), adapted with LoRA (on `q_proj`/`v_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`, r=64, α=64) |
| **Trainable params** | 82.1M / ~8.2B (1.0%) |
| **Optimizer** | AdamW (β=(0.9, 0.98), weight decay 0.001) |
| **LR schedule** | Cosine annealing (max LR 2e-4, min LR 1e-6, 500 warmup steps) |
| **Batching** | Dynamic, bucketed by audio duration (27 buckets) |
| **Steps** | 100,000 |
| **Gradient clipping** | 1.0 |
| **Strategy** | FSDP2 (full sharding), activation checkpointing on the LLM (to allow for long sequences), 1 node × 4 H100 |
| **Precision** | bf16 |

The model was trained for 100k steps and drew from a weighted, randomly-ordered, sharded mix of that dataset,
bucketed by duration into 27 buckets (up to 1,200s / 16,384 audio-equivalent tokens per example) with a
matching dynamic batch size per bucket (238 down to 1).

Validation covered CommonVoice ASR (fr/en/ar),
Multilingual TEDx speech translation (fr→en), spoken QA (SLUE-SQA-5, VoxPopuli-QA, en/fr), and audio/music
captioning (AudioCaps, MusicCaps).

The training code and configs are available in the [Luciole-Audio-Training repository](https://github.com/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training). Training used an updated version of [NeMo/Speech 3.1](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech) which can be found in our [NeMo/Speech fork](https://github.com/linagora-labs/NeMo/tree/luciole_speech.3.1.0-rc0).

To evaluate our models and compare them with other open-weight Audio LLMs, we used [our fork of AudioBench](https://github.com/OpenLLM-France/AudioBench). We used a combination of datasets from AudioBench and datasets available in [our HF audio evaluation repository](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Evaluation-Dataset). You can find the full details and results on [our AudioBench leaderboard](https://openllm-france.github.io/AudioBench/).

Results for French and English only, as well as for ASR, AST, and QA tasks only:

As you can see, the model [OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0) performs well in French and English compared to other models.

## Using the model

### With vLLM

The exported checkpoint's `config.json` declares `"model_type": "nemo_speechlm"` and
`"architectures": ["NeMoSpeechLMForConditionalGeneration"]`. Both are registered with vLLM by the SALM
plugin that ships inside `nemo-toolkit`
([`nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech/tree/main/nemo/collections/speechlm2/vllm/salm))
via the `vllm.general_plugins` entry point:

```toml
[project.entry-points."vllm.general_plugins"]
nemo_speechlm = "nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm:register"
```

vLLM auto-discovers this plugin at startup as soon as `nemo-toolkit` and `vllm` are installed in the same
environment. The plugin merges the
LoRA adapters into the LLM backbone on load and runs the frozen Parakeet encoder + connector to turn each
`<|audio|>` tag into the right number of audio-embedding slots before generation.

**Install using uv**

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate

uv pip install "nemo-toolkit[speechlm2,tts] @ git+https://github.com/linagora-labs/NeMo.git@luciole-1b-vllm-nemotron-fix"
uv pip install vllm==0.28.0
uv pip install "numpy<=2.4"
```

**Serve**

```bash
vllm serve OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0 \
    --max-model-len 16384
```

**Query** (OpenAI-compatible chat API, audio sent as base64):

```python
import base64
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

with open("sample.wav", "rb") as f:   # 16 kHz mono
    audio_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Transcris cet audio en français : <|audio|>"},
                {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": audio_b64, "format": "wav"}},
            ],
        }
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

The `<|audio|>` placeholder is the same `audio_locator_tag` used during training: put it in the text
wherever the audio should be attended to; the plugin expands it automatically. Audio must be 16 kHz mono;
the encoder supports chunked processing for long-form audio (well beyond the durations seen in training).

### With NeMo

The checkpoint can also be loaded directly with NeMo's `SALM` class
([`nemo.collections.speechlm2.models.salm`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech/blob/main/nemo/collections/speechlm2/models/salm.py)).

**Install**

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate

uv pip install "nemo-toolkit[speechlm2,tts] @ git+https://github.com/linagora-labs/NeMo.git@luciole-1b-vllm-nemotron-fix"
```

**Load and generate:**

```python
import torch
from nemo.collections.speechlm2 import SALM

model = SALM.from_pretrained("OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0")  # or a local checkpoint directory
model = model.eval().to(torch.bfloat16).to("cuda")

# High-level API: pass the audio file path(s) directly in the prompt, next to the
# `<|audio|>` placeholder; SALM loads and resamples the audio for you.
answer_ids = model.generate(
    prompts=[
        [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": f"Transcris cet audio en français : {model.audio_locator_tag}",
                "audio": ["sample.wav"],
            }
        ]
    ],
    max_new_tokens=256,
)
print(model.tokenizer.ids_to_text(answer_ids[0].tolist()))
```

A prompt can carry several turns and several audio clips (one `<|audio|>` tag per clip, in order).

### Example prompts for each task

- ASR: 
  - English: `Make a word-for-word transcription in English of the spoken content.`
  - French: `Fais une transcription mot pour mot en français du contenu parlé.`
  - German: `Erstelle eine wortwörtliche Transkription des gesprochenen Inhalts auf Deutsch.`
  - Spanish: `Haz una transcripción palabra por palabra en español del contenido hablado.`
  - Italian: `Fai una trascrizione parola per parola in italiano del contenuto parlato.`
  - Portuguese: `Faça uma transcrição palavra por palavra em português do conteúdo falado.`
  - Dutch: `Maak een woord-voor-woord transcriptie in het Nederlands van de gesproken inhoud.`
  - No language given: `Can you write the text of this audio file in its source language?`
- QA: `Listen to the audio and answer the question.`
- AST: `Translate this file into French.`
- Diarization: 
  - `Provide a time-stamped, speaker-attributed transcript of this audio.`
  - `Transcris et diarise cet enregistrement, avec les horodatages de chaque tour.`

## Model Description

**Luciole-1B-Audio-1.0** is an audio-capable version of [Luciole-1B-Instruct-1.1](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-1B-Instruct-1.1).
The model was developed by [LINAGORA](https://linagora.com) and
the [OpenLLM-France](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France) consortium, as part of the OpenLLM France project funded by
[BPI France](https://www.bpifrance.fr/) under the France 2030 program.

The training of Luciole-1B-Audio-1.0 was conducted on the Jean Zay supercomputer managed by [IDRIS](http://www.idris.fr/docs/idris/missions),
using the [NVIDIA NeMo Speech](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech) toolkit.
The model was trained on various tasks and types of audio, including ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition), AST (Automatic Speech Translation), QA (Question Answering), Sound (Question Answering and Captioning), Music (Question Answering and Captioning) and more.

If you are looking for the best compromise between speed and performance go check the [Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-8B-Audio-1.0).

### Bias, Risks, and Limitations

- Inherits the limitations of the base [Luciole-1B-Instruct-1.1](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-1B-Instruct-1.1)
  language model: it can struggle with math word problems and is susceptible to hallucination.
- Training sequences were capped at 16,384 tokens (audio and text combined), so longer contexts are untested.
<!-- - The audio encoder and its front-end were entirely frozen during training, so audio understanding is bounded by what
  Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 already hears: the model cannot learn to compensate for acoustic conditions the
  encoder itself handles poorly. -->
- Language coverage is uneven. French and English make up most of the training mix and are the only languages seen on every task. German, Spanish and Italian were seen in training for ASR, AST and spoken QA. Portuguese, Dutch and Arabic for ASR and AST only.
- Arabic is the weakest language: the frozen Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 encoder was not trained on Arabic,
  so the model is unreliable there (FLEURS WER ~69%).
<!-- - LoRA fine-tuning only touches attention projections in the LLM; no additional audio-specific safety or
  refusal tuning was performed beyond what the base LLM already has. -->

### Recommendations

- Speech, sound and music understanding (summarization, captioning, sound/music QA, conversation):
  best in French and English, the only languages the model was trained on for these tasks.
- Transcription (ASR) and translation (AST): supported in French, English, German, Spanish,
  Italian, Portuguese and Dutch. For production ASR/AST pipelines, a dedicated model may still
  perform better.
- Spoken question answering: mainly supported in French and English. German, Spanish and
  Italian are also supported, but with far less training data.
- Other languages and tasks: outside French and English, evaluate the model on your own data
  before relying on it, especially for a task the model was not trained on in that language.
- Up-to-date or domain-specific knowledge: as with the base LLM, pair the model with a RAG
  pipeline.

## Training details

### Training data

Trained on the [OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training-Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training-Dataset),
a large multilingual, multi-task collection of audio–text conversations comprising: ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition),
AST (Automatic Speech Translation), spoken question answering, summarization, diarization, temporal localization,
speaker/gender/age/emotion/language recognition, and music/sound captioning and QA (Question Answering).

### Instruction template

Same chat template as the base LLM (inspired by Qwen3), extended with an `<|audio|>` locator tag:
wherever `<|audio|>` appears in a turn, the corresponding audio segment is encoded and its embeddings
replace the tag before the sequence reaches the LLM. Conversations can carry several audio clips and mix
audio-only, text-only, and audio+text turns within the same dialogue (see the
[dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training-Dataset) for example
conversations).

### Training Procedure

| Component | Details |
|---|---|
| **Audio encoder** | [Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3) Conformer encoder, frozen |
| **RoTE** | Applied between audio encoder and audio adapter. θ=1200, rotary fraction=0.2. Inspired by [Goel et al., 2024, OMCAT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12109).|
| **Audio adapter** | Linear projection into the LLM embedding space (1024 -> 2048) |
| **LLM** | [Luciole-1B-Instruct-1.1](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-1B-Instruct-1.1), adapted with LoRA (on `q_proj`/`v_proj`, r=64, α=64) |
| **Trainable params** | 12.3M / ~1.9B (0.6%) |
| **Optimizer** | AdamW (β=(0.9, 0.98), weight decay 0.001) |
| **LR schedule** | Cosine annealing (max LR 2e-4, min LR 1e-6, 500 warmup steps) |
| **Batching** | Dynamic, bucketed by audio duration (27 buckets) |
| **Steps** | 100,000 |
| **Gradient clipping** | 1.0 |
| **Strategy** | DDP, 1 node × 4 H100 |
| **Precision** | bf16 |

The model was trained for 100k steps and drew from a weighted, randomly-ordered, sharded mix of that dataset,
bucketed by duration into 27 buckets (up to 1,200s / 16,384 audio-equivalent tokens per example) with a
matching dynamic batch size per bucket (238 down to 1).

Validation covered CommonVoice ASR (fr/en/ar),
Multilingual TEDx speech translation (fr→en), spoken QA (SLUE-SQA-5, VoxPopuli-QA, en/fr), and audio/music
captioning (AudioCaps, MusicCaps).

The training code and configs are available in the [Luciole-Audio-Training repository](https://github.com/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Training). Training used an updated version of [NeMo/Speech 3.1](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech) which can be found in our [NeMo/Speech fork](https://github.com/linagora-labs/NeMo/tree/luciole_speech.3.1.0-rc0).

## Evaluation

To evaluate our models and compare them with other open-weight Audio LLMs, we used [our fork of AudioBench](https://github.com/OpenLLM-France/AudioBench). We used a combination of datasets from AudioBench and datasets available in [our HF audio evaluation repository](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-Audio-Evaluation-Dataset). You can find the full details and results on [our AudioBench leaderboard](https://openllm-france.github.io/AudioBench/).

A small excerpt from the leaderboard, showing the main table across all tasks and languages:

![results.png](assets/results.png)

Results for French and English only, as well as for ASR, AST, and QA tasks only:

![results_fr_en.png](assets/results_fr_en.png)

As you can see, the model [OpenLLM-France/Luciole-1B-Audio-1.0](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Luciole-1B-Audio-1.0) performs well in French and English compared to other models of similar size.

Ming-3.0-audio-flash

Hear clearly. Understand deeply. Act intelligently.

Ming-3.0-audio-flash is a native audio-language model from inclusionAI. It accepts audio together with text instructions and supports speech recognition, spoken question answering, audio understanding, audio reasoning, and optional synthesized-speech responses.
GitHub · 🤖 ModelScope · 🤗 Flash · 🤗 Tiny · 💻 Examples
## Model Summary | Property | Description | | --- | --- | | Developer | inclusionAI | | Model type | Native audio-language Mixture-of-Experts model | | Parameters | 126B total parameters, 6.5B activated per inference step | | Inputs | Audio and text instructions | | Outputs | Text, or text with optional synthesized speech | | Primary languages | Chinese and English, including varied accents and dialects | | License | MIT | ## Highlights - **Complex speech recognition:** Handles Chinese and English speech, dialects, accents, noisy environments, and multi-speaker recordings. - **Long-audio understanding:** Comprehends and analyzes long-form recordings. - **Multidimensional perception:** Understands speech, non-speech sounds, acoustic scenes, and music. - **Audio reasoning:** Answers questions and performs reasoning over audio content. - **Audio interaction:** Produces text responses and can optionally synthesize speech with built-in voices or a reference voice. ## Architecture Ming-3.0-audio-flash combines an audio encoder and projector with a Mixture-of-Experts language backbone. An optional Talker generates speech responses from the model's output.

## Quick Start with Transformers The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the repository code before enabling `trust_remote_code=True`. ```bash git clone https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash.git cd Ming-3.0-audio-flash python -m venv .venv-transformers source .venv-transformers/bin/activate pip install -r requirements-transformers.txt ``` ### Audio Understanding ```bash python examples/transformers_audio.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --prompt "Please answer the question in the audio." ``` ### Speech Recognition ```bash python examples/transformers_audio.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --task asr \ --max-new-tokens 256 \ --no-repeat-ngram-size 10 ``` The validated ASR prompt asks the model to identify the spoken language and place a tab between the language label and transcription. ### Direct Python Usage ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash" audio_path = "examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, use_fast=False, ) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True, ).eval() messages = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio", "audio": audio_path}, {"type": "text", "text": "Please answer the question in the audio."}, ], } ] inputs = processor(messages).to(model.device) inputs["audio_feats"] = inputs["audio_feats"].to(model.dtype) with torch.inference_mode(): output_ids = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False, ) generated_ids = output_ids[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :] response = processor.decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens=True).strip() print(response) ``` ## Speech Output The Talker example supports built-in voices and reference-audio voice prompting: ```bash python examples/transformers_thinker_talker.py \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --audio examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --voice US_Stella \ --output output.wav ``` See the [voice guide](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/docs/voices.md) for available voice names and reference-audio usage. ## Serving ### vLLM-Omni ```bash export MODEL_PATH=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash MING_OUTPUT_MODE=text ./scripts/serve_vllm_omni.sh "$MODEL_PATH" ``` The reference 128K serving profile uses tensor parallelism across eight 80 GB H800 GPUs. Select the deployment YAML that matches text-only or Talker output. See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/README.md#vllm-omni) for details. # MiniMax Music 3 TurboSpark, 4-bit, 8-step

A TurboSpark-compatible MiniMax Music 3 checkpoint for local Apple Silicon music generation. It combines the pinned `mlx-community/MiniMax-Music3-4bit` checkpoint with the community 8-step Turbo LoRA. The adapter is merged into the model's target matrices as FP16; the untouched affine INT4 group-64 linears remain quantized.

TurboSpark's native Rust/Metal runtime reads the model variant metadata in `config.json` and selects 8-step Euler sampling when the caller leaves the step count unspecified. The TurboSpark macOS app installs this exact repository revision through its pinned audio catalog. This is a merged checkpoint for the app, not an adapter-only download.

## Provenance and prior work

The 4-bit base is [`mlx-community/MiniMax-Music3-4bit`](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/MiniMax-Music3-4bit), pinned at commit `c7ea32923b245fe5afc22d740a1936ad2ac590f3`.

The adapter comes from [guillaume127/MiniMax-Music-3-Turbo-FP8](https://huggingface.co/guillaume127/MiniMax-Music-3-Turbo-FP8), specifically `minimax_music3_turbo_lora_8step.safetensors`. Its prior-art implementation and training details are in [Guillaume-127/Minimax-music-3-Turbo-8-steps](https://github.com/Guillaume-127/Minimax-music-3-Turbo-8-steps). TurboSpark did not train this adapter. Adapter SHA-256: `9722bb8da08da3912a2b6b8fdb173b9d7d4ce01a68818114a8218cfe25d8545a`. The tested adapter-only MLX package is [`cowWhySo/MiniMax-Music3-Turbo-MLX-LoRA`](https://huggingface.co/cowWhySo/MiniMax-Music3-Turbo-MLX-LoRA/tree/26c94413b40fbb26ebd034a4d05f027f7429194f).

The rank-64, alpha-64 adapter targets the DiT in all 36 transformer blocks. Its fused QKV up-projection is split across Q, K, and V, yielding 216 residual projections. TurboSpark's merge probe covered all 216 targets; the report is in `merge-report.json`.

## Use with TurboSpark

Install the model through TurboSpark's MiniMax Music 3 model picker. The app uses its immutable catalog pin and runs the native Rust/Metal backend. No Python or MLX runtime is needed in TurboSpark.

The project is [whit3rabbit/turbospark](https://github.com/whit3rabbit/turbospark). The checkpoint's metadata selects 8-step Euler with reference guidance. An explicit step count supplied by the caller still overrides that recommendation.

## Evaluation status

This is an experimental checkpoint. One blind 15-second vocal comparison at seed 23 was judged similar to the 30-step reference; the 8-step no-adapter control was judged noticeably thinner. The adapter run took 55.18 seconds of process wall time on the test machine. This single seed does not establish broad audio quality, long-form behavior, or a stable performance result. Evaluate lyrics, genres, seeds, and 30–120 second generations before treating it as production-qualified.

## Model size

The two merged weight shards are 12,671,777,748 bytes in the model index. The full local repository is about 12.68 GB decimal. The 216 adapted target matrices are FP16; all unaffected affine INT4 group-64 linears remain packed.

## License

The checkpoint is a derivative of MiniMax Music 3 and remains subject to the [MiniMax Music 3 Community License](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3/blob/main/LICENSE), including its acceptable-use and commercial terms. The source adapter repository declares Apache-2.0 for its adapter. Review both sources and their conditions before use or redistribution. The original MiniMax license is included as `LICENSE`.

Ming-3.0-audio-tiny

Hear clearly. Understand deeply. Act intelligently.

Ming-3.0-audio-tiny is a compact native audio-language model from inclusionAI. It accepts audio together with text instructions and supports speech recognition, spoken question answering, audio understanding, audio reasoning, and optional synthesized-speech responses.
GitHub · 🤖 ModelScope · 🤗 Flash · 🤗 Tiny · 💻 Examples
## Model Summary | Property | Description | | --- | --- | | Developer | inclusionAI | | Model type | Compact native audio-language Mixture-of-Experts model | | Parameters | 9.3B total parameters, 2.7B activated per inference step | | Inputs | Audio and text instructions | | Outputs | Text, or text with optional synthesized speech | | Primary languages | Chinese and English, including varied accents and dialects | | License | MIT | ## Highlights - **Efficient audio intelligence:** Provides speech and audio understanding in a compact Mixture-of-Experts model. - **Complex speech recognition:** Handles Chinese and English speech, dialects, accents, noisy environments, and multi-speaker recordings. - **Long-audio understanding:** Comprehends and analyzes long-form recordings. - **Multidimensional perception:** Understands speech, non-speech sounds, acoustic scenes, and music. - **Audio reasoning:** Answers questions and performs reasoning over audio content. - **Audio interaction:** Produces text responses and can optionally synthesize speech with built-in voices or a reference voice. ## Architecture Ming-3.0-audio-tiny combines an audio encoder and projector with a compact Mixture-of-Experts language backbone. An optional Talker generates speech responses from the model's output. ## Quick Start with Transformers The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the repository code before enabling `trust_remote_code=True`. ```bash git clone https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash.git cd Ming-3.0-audio-flash python -m venv .venv-transformers source .venv-transformers/bin/activate pip install -r requirements-transformers.txt ``` ### Audio Understanding ```bash python examples/transformers_audio.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny \ --prompt "Please answer the question in the audio." ``` ### Speech Recognition ```bash python examples/transformers_audio.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny \ --task asr \ --max-new-tokens 256 \ --no-repeat-ngram-size 10 ``` The validated ASR prompt asks the model to identify the spoken language and place a tab between the language label and transcription. ### Direct Python Usage ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny" audio_path = "examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, use_fast=False, ) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True, ).eval() messages = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio", "audio": audio_path}, {"type": "text", "text": "Please answer the question in the audio."}, ], } ] inputs = processor(messages).to(model.device) inputs["audio_feats"] = inputs["audio_feats"].to(model.dtype) with torch.inference_mode(): output_ids = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False, ) generated_ids = output_ids[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :] response = processor.decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens=True).strip() print(response) ``` ## Speech Output The Talker example supports built-in voices and reference-audio voice prompting: ```bash python examples/transformers_thinker_talker.py \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny \ --audio examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --voice US_Stella \ --output output.wav ``` See the [voice guide](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/docs/voices.md) for available voice names, invocation rules, and reference-audio usage. ## Serving ### vLLM-Omni Text output or ASR uses the Tiny Thinker on one GPU: ```bash export MODEL_PATH=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny MING_MODEL_VARIANT=tiny MING_OUTPUT_MODE=text \ ./scripts/serve_vllm_omni.sh "$MODEL_PATH" ``` For synthesized-speech output, select the full-audio profile: ```bash export MODEL_PATH=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny MING_MODEL_VARIANT=tiny MING_OUTPUT_MODE=audio \ ./scripts/serve_vllm_omni.sh "$MODEL_PATH" ``` The reference full-audio profile places the Thinker on GPU 0 and the Talker on GPU 1. Select the deployment YAML that matches text-only, ASR, or Talker output. See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/README.md#vllm-omni) for details. Select an IP or registered voice with the vLLM-Omni client's `--voice` option: ```bash python examples/vllm_omni_audio_chat.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --audio-response \ --voice US_Stella \ --output-audio outputs/answer.wav ``` The client sends this selection as Chat Completions `audio.voice: {"id": "..."}`. vLLM-Omni uses the built-in IP voice `灵小柔` when no voice is specified. The model directory also provides `灵楷` and `US_James` as preset reference voices under `voice_presets/voice_audio/`, with their matching transcripts in `voice_presets/voice_prompts.json`. Both names are also available as built-in IP voices. ### SGLang ```bash export MODEL_PATH=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny MING_MODEL_VARIANT=tiny CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ ./scripts/serve_sglang.sh "$MODEL_PATH" ``` The validated Tiny SGLang profile uses one GPU and provides text output. See the [SGLang example](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/examples/sglang_audio_chat.py) for client usage. ### SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/) serves transcription, audio chat, and speech synthesis from one server. The Tiny checkpoint fits on a single GPU; `--talker.gpu 0` colocates speech synthesis with the other stages: ```bash sgl-omni serve --model-path inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-tiny --talker.gpu 0 ``` The server exposes OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/speech`, and `/v1/chat/completions` endpoints. The [SGLang-Omni cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming3_audio.html) shows client examples; the same requests work with the Tiny model name. ## Evaluation The shared benchmark figures below include results for both Ming-3.0-audio-tiny and Ming-3.0-audio-flash. ### Speech Recognition

Ming-3.0-tts-tiny

7.9B-A1.3B multilingual MoE speech synthesis with paralinguistic and free-form control.

GitHub | Blog & Demos | ModelScope

This repository contains **Ming-3.0-tts-tiny**, the Ming-3.0-tts mixture-of-experts checkpoint built on Ling V3. Its Ling V3 backbone has 7.9B total parameters and activates about 1.3B parameters per token. The repository includes sharded weights, supporting model code, audio tokenizer, speaker encoder and text tokenizer. > **Inference requires the [Ming-3.0-tts GitHub repository](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts).** This Hugging Face repository is for checkpoint distribution and does not provide a standalone inference setup. Clone the GitHub repository and follow its README for the current dependencies, inference code and usage instructions. The CLI scripts and Python APIs referenced below are provided by the GitHub repository. ## Model Details | Item | Value | | --- | --- | | Architecture | Mixture of Experts, Ling V3 backbone | | Backbone parameters | 7.9B total, about 1.3B active per token | | Languages | Chinese, English, German, Spanish, French, Korean, Japanese | | Dialects | Sichuanese, Cantonese | | Python API | `ming_tiny.MingTinyTTS` | | CLI | `infer_tiny.py` | | Prompt protocol | `thinking_v1` | ## Capabilities - Zero-shot voice cloning from a short reference clip - Voice Design from a natural-language speaker description - Free-form control of delivery and speaking style - 100+ built-in Chinese voices and five built-in English voices - Multilingual synthesis and Sichuanese/Cantonese dialect control - 14 inline tags for breath, cough, sigh, laughter, hesitation, surprise and question/confirmation sounds in Chinese or English - Explicit emotion, speed, pitch and volume control - Multi-speaker dialogue from a script and speaker references (`podcast`)

## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash git clone https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts.git cd Ming-3.0-tts conda create -n ming-tiny python=3.10.15 -y conda activate ming-tiny pip install -r requirements-tiny.txt ``` Tiny uses a separate reference inference environment: Python **3.10.15**, PyTorch and torchaudio **2.7.1+cu118** (CUDA 11.8 wheels), and `transformers==4.46.3`. Install the pinned dependencies from [requirements-tiny.txt](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts/blob/main/requirements-tiny.txt) in a dedicated environment, as other dependency versions differ from 0.5B. We recommend using NVIDIA H800 for inference. ### Download ```bash pip install "huggingface_hub[cli]" hf download inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny --local-dir Ming-3.0-tts-tiny ``` ### CLI Inference ```bash python infer_tiny.py \ --model_path inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny \ --task dialect \ --text "今日天气几好，我哋食完饭一齐去海边行下啦。" \ --dialect 广粤话 \ --prompt_wav data/wavs/10002287-00000094.wav \ --output_path output/tiny.wav ``` ### Python API Loading configures the release runtime (bf16, portable MoE loop, fp32 recurrent state) and checks the checkpoint against it; `generate()` defaults to `cfg_scale=2.0`, `temperature=0`, `flow_steps=10`, and `sigma=0.25`. ```python from ming_tiny import MingTinyTTS tts = MingTinyTTS.from_pretrained("inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny", device="cuda:0") tts.generate( task="seed", text="傍晚的风从山口吹过来，远处的云慢慢染成了金色。", prompt_wav="data/wavs/10002287-00000094.wav", prompt_text="在此奉劝大家别乱打美白针。", target_language="Chinese", # English for English text output_path="outputs/seed.wav", ) ``` ### Supported Tasks Each call selects one task and accepts the inputs listed below: | Task | Reference audio | Reference text | `target_language` | Controls | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `seed` | one | required | `Chinese` / `English`, required | — | | `multilingual` | one | required | `German` / `Spanish` / `French` / `Korean` / `Japanese` | — | | `paralinguistic` | one | required | `Chinese` / `English` | inline tags in `text` | | `podcast` | one per speaker | one per speaker, same order | inferred from the text | `speaker_N:` at the start of every line | | `basic` | one | not accepted | — | `speed`, `pitch`, `volume`, all three | | `emotion` | one | not accepted | — | `emotion` | | `dialect` | one | not accepted | — | `dialect`: `川渝话` / `广粤话` | | `freeform` | one | not accepted | — | `instruction` | | `voice_design` | none | — | — | `style` | | `ip` | none | — | — | `ip` | Freeform always requires a reference clip and cannot be combined with voice design, a built-in voice, emotion, dialect or attribute controls. For `podcast`, start every dialogue line with `speaker_N:` and provide one reference audio clip and transcript per speaker, in speaker order. Repeat `--prompt_wav` and `--prompt_text` on the command line. See the [Tiny examples](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts#ming-30-tts-tiny) for a Podcast Python example and [examples/one_click/](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts/tree/main/examples/one_click) for scripts for every task. `python infer_tiny.py --help` lists the CLI arguments. ### Verify the Checkpoint ```bash python tools/preflight_tiny.py --model_path /path/to/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny ``` ## Serving with SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/) serves this checkpoint on one GPU: ```bash sgl-omni serve --model-path inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny ``` Synthesize speech through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny", "input": "Get the trust fund to the bank early.", "response_format": "wav", "seed": 123 }' \ --output speech.wav ``` `response_format` accepts `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`, and `pcm`. For zero-shot voice cloning, pass `ref_audio` (a server-side path or a `data:` URL) together with `ref_text`, the transcript of the reference recording. # KittenTTS 2

A 1.7B speech language model with in-context voice cloning. It reads text and writes S3
codec tokens, which a vocoder turns into 24 kHz audio.

```bash
pip install kittenml
```

```python
from kittenml import KittenTTS
import soundfile as sf

m = KittenTTS("KittenML/kitten-tts-2")

# a built-in voice
audio = m.generate("One day, a little girl named Lily found a needle in her room.",
                   voice="Bruno")

# or clone one, from 5-30 seconds of a single speaker
audio = m.generate("This is my own voice.", reference="my_voice.wav")

sf.write("output.wav", audio, m.sample_rate)
```

Everything the model needs is in this repository, so no Hugging Face login is required.

## Voices

`m.available_voices` lists all 47. Bella, Jasper, Luna, Bruno, Rosie, Hugo, Kiki
and Leo are the same speakers as in KittenTTS 0.8, so existing code keeps working.

Nine are named after a language rather than a person — Arabic, Chinese, French, German,
Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish — and are how you reach those languages,
since the voice is what carries the accent:

```python
m.generate("Guten Morgen. Ich wünsche dir einen wunderschönen Tag.",
           voice="German", normalize=False)
```

Pass `normalize=False` for non-English text: the text normalizer is English-tuned and
will mangle numbers and dates in other languages.

## Expression controls

> **Beta.** Emotion control steers delivery rather than guaranteeing it, and the effect
> varies by voice and by sentence.

```python
m.generate("[joyful] We won the grant <laugh> I can (((hardly))) believe it!",
           voice="Kiki", preset="expressive")
```

A leading `[emotion]` tag, inline `<event>` tags and `(((emphasis)))` spans reach the
model as markup rather than being spoken, and switch on its expression conditioning.

**Emotions** — one leading tag sets the emotion for the whole line:

`[angry]` `[contemplative]` `[excited]` `[joyful]` `[mundane]`
`[nervous]` `[sad]` `[stern]` `[surprised]` `[tender]`

**Vocal events** — inline, anywhere in the line:

`<gasp>` `<giggle>` `<growl>` `<gulp>` `<laugh>`
`<pause>` `<scoff>` `<sigh>` `<sob>` `<um>`

**Emphasis** — triple parentheses stress a word or short phrase:

```python
m.generate("I told you (((never))) to open that door.", voice="Victor")
```

Only these twenty tags are recognised. They are the most common of the many in the
training data, so a rarer one such as `[reverent]` is spoken as ordinary text rather
than treated as markup — as is anything else bracketed, like `section [3]` or `x < 5`.

## Weight variants

The language model ships in three packings of the same weights. `weights=` picks one;
`model.available_weights` lists them.

| `weights=` | On disk | |
|---|---|---|
| `"packed"` *(default)* | 954 MB | 1.58-bit ternary body, bf16 embedding. **Lossless** |
| `"emb4"` | 469 MB | Same body in TL2, plus a 4-bit embedding. **Lossy** |
| `"full"` | 3469 MB | Plain bf16 |

```python
m = KittenTTS("KittenML/kitten-tts-2", weights="emb4")
```

Only the variant you ask for is downloaded.

`emb4` halves the download, and the saving is almost entirely the token embedding — 324M
parameters that `packed` has to leave at bf16 because they are not ternary. Its transformer
body is still bit-exact; the embedding is not, at L2 relative error 0.118 against bf16.
Measured at export, that costs roughly a tenth of a point of perplexity on internal
evaluations. Small, but it is the one lossy thing here, which is why `packed` stays the
default.

## Decoders

Audio is decoded in two stages, and the first can be swapped for a smaller distilled
student with weights packed to 4 or 8 bits:

```python
m = KittenTTS("KittenML/kitten-tts-2", decoder="student_w4")
```

| Decoder | Flow on disk | |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | 459 MB | Best quality |
| `student_w4` | 39 MB | Distilled single-step student, weights packed to 4 bits |

These trade fidelity for footprint, not for speed: quantisation shrinks storage and
memory bandwidth, not arithmetic.

## What is in here

```
lm/          the speech language model, plus its spk_proj speaker head
speaker/     the speaker-embedding model used when cloning
voices/      reference clips, transcripts, and precomputed embeddings
decoders/    the optional 4-bit decoder
cpp/         GGUF weights for the llama.cpp fork, see "Running on CPU"
config.json  token layout, decode presets, voice and decoder indexes
```

The weights are 947 MiB: 910 MiB for the language model and 37 MiB for the decoder.
A load pulls those rather than the whole repository, and only the decoder you ask for.

The language model's linear weights are ternary — within every 128-wide group each
value is exactly one of `{-scale, 0, +scale}` — so bf16 spends 16 bits to say one of
three things. `lm/model-ternary.safetensors` packs them five trits to a byte, 1.6 bits
per weight, with each group keeping its scale at full precision:

| | |
|---|---|
| `lm/model.safetensors` | 3.47 GB, bf16 throughout |
| `lm/model-ternary.safetensors` | **0.95 GB**, the same weights, 3.6x smaller |

The packing is exact rather than approximate, so the two produce bit-identical audio.
`config.json` points `lm_packed` at the smaller file and that is what gets downloaded;
the full file stays for anything loading this with plain `transformers`.

## Running on CPU

KittenTTS 2 runs on CPU out of the box — `device` is auto-detected — but the fastest way
is [kitten-tts-2-cpp](https://github.com/KittenML/kitten-tts-2-cpp), our llama.cpp fork.
The `cpp/` directory here holds what it needs: the GGUF language model and its decoders.

## Requirements

Python 3.10 or later, and PyTorch.

loads this repository, under Apache 2.0.

# FireRedTTS3-Instruct for SGLang Omni

We provide our FireRedTTS3-Instruct checkpoint for inference with
[SGLang Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni). It supports
reference-audio voice cloning, instruction-guided voice design, semantic editing, and acoustic editing.
Audio output is 24 kHz mono, with WAV responses and streaming PCM available
through the `/v1/audio/speech` API.

Our model code and original checkpoint release:

- [FireRedTTS3 source code](https://github.com/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3)
- [Original FireRedTTS3 weights and model card](https://huggingface.co/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3)

This card documents the SGLang Omni loading and serving workflow.

## Install SGLang Omni

Use Linux with an NVIDIA CUDA GPU and Python 3.12. Follow the
[SGLang Omni installation guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/get_started/installation.md)
for the CUDA, UCX, and FlashAttention prerequisites, then install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni.git
cd sglang-omni
pip install uv
uv venv .venv -p 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install --prerelease=allow -e '.[firered-tts3]'
```

Use a revision containing the FireRedTTS3 integration. Before that integration
is merged, check out the corresponding PR revision before installing; an older
PyPI release or checkout does not provide this model. Run the following commands
from the `sglang-omni` repository root.

## Download this checkpoint

For PR testing, use our temporary checkpoint at
[CKermit/FireRedTTS3-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/CKermit/FireRedTTS3-Instruct).
After this PR, we plan to publish the official checkpoint at
[FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3-Instruct).

```bash
hf download CKermit/FireRedTTS3-Instruct \
  --local-dir ./models/FireRedTTS3-Instruct
```

Download the complete repository, including configuration, tokenizer, and
`redae/` assets. Loading only the root
`model.safetensors` file is insufficient. If you already have the complete
checkpoint locally, use that directory directly.

## Start the server

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 sgl-omni serve \
  --model-path ./models/FireRedTTS3-Instruct \
  --config examples/configs/firered_tts3_instruct.yaml \
  --allowed-local-media-path "$PWD/docs/_static/audio" \
  --port 8000
```

Wait for `/health` to return HTTP 200 before sending requests. Initial model
loading, compilation, and warmup can take several minutes.

The reference clips below are included in the SGLang Omni repository. Local
paths are resolved on the **server**, relative to its working directory.
For your own clips, allow their directory with `--allowed-local-media-path`
and supply the matching transcript for cloning.

## Voice cloning

Provide exactly one reference recording and its actual transcript. The example
uses the repository's `ref_voice.wav`:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "FireRedTTS3-Instruct",
    "input": "Hello, welcome to SGLang Omni.",
    "language": "English",
    "references": [{
      "audio_path": "docs/_static/audio/ref_voice.wav",
      "text": "It was the night before my birthday. Hooray! It’s almost here! It may not be a holiday, but it’s the best day of the year."
    }],
    "seed": 42
  }' --output clone.wav
```

Omit `task_type` for cloning, or set it to `Base`. The value `tts` is not an
accepted serving task name.

## Voice design

Generate a voice from a description, without a reference recording:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "FireRedTTS3-Instruct",
    "input": "今天天气很好，我们一起去公园散步吧。",
    "task_type": "VoiceDesign",
    "instructions": "一个年轻女性的温柔嗓音，语速稍慢，带一点俏皮。",
    "seed": 42
  }' --output voice_design.wav
```

## Semantic editing

Use the reference recording as the source to edit. Its content supplies the
input, so `input` may be empty; no reference transcript is required:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @- --output semantic_edit.wav <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "FireRedTTS3-Instruct",
  "input": "",
  "task_type": "SemanticEdit",
  "instructions": "Replace 'birthday' with 'anniversary'.",
  "ref_audio": "docs/_static/audio/ref_voice.wav",
  "seed": 42
}
JSON
```

For substitutions, use the quoted form `Replace 'source' with 'target'.`
The quoted example above was verified by transcribing the generated audio;
omitting the quotes did not perform the intended replacement in this test.
The `x-gen-text` response header contains text with edit masks, so the target
word may appear only in the audio. Validate the rendered audio rather than
requiring the target word to appear in that header.

## Acoustic editing

Adjust the source recording's speed, pitch, or volume. This example requests
0.8x speed through the model's native acoustic-edit task:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "FireRedTTS3-Instruct",
    "input": "",
    "task_type": "AcousticEdit",
    "ref_audio": "docs/_static/audio/ref_voice.wav",
    "speed": 0.8,
    "seed": 42
  }' --output acoustic_edit.wav
```

Raw acoustic instructions must follow the trained templates rather than
free-form descriptions. For pitch or volume, use, for example,
`"instructions": "shift the pitch by 2 steps"` or
`"instructions": "adjust the volume to 0.8"`. An explicit `instructions`
string takes precedence over the composed speed instruction. The `speed`
field applies to `AcousticEdit`; it does not change cloning or voice design.
Edit sources are capped at 20 seconds. VoiceDesign and SemanticEdit generate
text before audio, so their first-audio latency differs from cloning.

## Streaming

To stream audio, add `"stream": true` and `"response_format": "pcm"` to
the request and use `curl -N`. The response contains raw **24 kHz, signed
16-bit little-endian, mono PCM**. Save it as `output.pcm` and convert it with:

```bash
ffmpeg -f s16le -ar 24000 -ac 1 -i output.pcm output.wav
```

The server also exposes `/v1/audio/speech/stream` over WebSocket. See the
[WebSocket protocol](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/basic_usage/tts.md#websocket-speech-streaming)
for `session.config`, `input.text`, `input.commit`, and `input.done` events.

## Offline Python SDK

Save this as `offline_tts.py` in the SGLang Omni repository root and run
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python offline_tts.py`. This starts the pipeline
locally without an HTTP server.

```python
import asyncio
import multiprocessing as mp
from pathlib import Path

from sglang_omni.client import Client, GenerateRequest
from sglang_omni.models.firered_tts3.config import FireRedTTS3PipelineConfig
from sglang_omni.pipeline.mp_runner import MultiProcessPipelineRunner


async def main() -> None:
    config = FireRedTTS3PipelineConfig(
        model_path="./models/FireRedTTS3-Instruct",
    )
    config.stage_named("talker").factory.flow_mode = "fp32"
    runner = MultiProcessPipelineRunner(config)
    await runner.start(timeout=600)
    try:
        client = Client(runner.coordinator)
        result = await client.speech(
            GenerateRequest(
                prompt={
                    "input": "今天天气很好，我们一起去公园散步吧。",
                    "task_type": "VoiceDesign",
                    "instructions": "一个年轻女性的温柔嗓音，语速稍慢，带一点俏皮。",
                    "seed": 42,
                },
                stream=False,
            ),
            request_id="demo-1",
        )
        Path("offline.wav").write_bytes(result.audio_bytes)
    finally:
        await runner.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mp.set_start_method("spawn", force=True)
    asyncio.run(main())
```

## Serving notes

- The current deployment supports a single GPU (`tp_size=1`).
- HTTP `input` is limited to 400 characters. Editing requests may use an empty
  `input` as shown above.
- Use an explicit language: `Chinese` (default), `English`, `Japanese`, `Korean`,
  `German`, `French`, `Russian`, `Portuguese`, `Spanish`, or `Italian`.
  Automatic language detection (`Auto`) is unsupported. These are the stock
  serving API's accepted language values; FireRedTTS3 supports additional
  languages and dialects through our standalone inference pipeline.
- Submit spoken-form text when normalization is needed. The FastText and LLM
  text-normalization setup in our standalone pipeline is not used in this quick start.
- Put flow-solver settings under `stage_params.talker`, for example
  `{"n_timesteps": 10, "inference_cfg": 2.0, "max_patches": 200}`. Unknown
  top-level fields are not forwarded as model settings.
- `seed` controls the per-request flow sampler. Different precisions, hardware,
  or batching schedules can produce different results with the same seed.
- For our published model-quality results, see the
  [FireRedTTS3 model card](https://huggingface.co/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3).
  SGLang Omni runtime accuracy and performance are evaluated separately.
- Keep the example Instruct configuration's `flow_mode: fp32` for the
  supported default. The offline example sets it explicitly because it does
  not load the example YAML.
- `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` affect the VoiceDesign/SemanticEdit text
  phase. They do not control continuous-latent audio generation.

See the [FireRedTTS3 cookbook](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/cookbook/firered_tts3.md)
for the full request parameters and deployment configuration.

- The project incorporates zero-shot voice cloning functionality; Please note that this capability is intended **solely for academic research purposes**.
- **DO NOT** use this model for **ANY illegal activities**❗️❗️

# Chatterbox Multilingual — GGUF

[ResembleAI's Chatterbox Multilingual](https://huggingface.co/ResembleAI/chatterbox): expressive speech in 23 languages, with voice cloning.

Two files make one model, as with llama.cpp's multimodal projectors: the **model** file is the text-to-speech LM backbone, run by [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp); the **codec** file holds the audio side (decoder / vocoder, speaker encoders and the adaptor between the two), run by [codec.cpp](https://github.com/mybigday/codec.cpp). The runtimes below wire the two graphs together, on CPU or GPU (CUDA, Vulkan, Metal), fully offline.

## Command line (codec.cpp)

With [codec.cpp](https://github.com/mybigday/codec.cpp)'s `tts-cli` ([build it](https://github.com/mybigday/codec.cpp#text-to-speech); it bundles llama.cpp), then:

```bash
hf download BricksDisplay/Chatterbox-Multilingual-TTS-GGUF chatterbox-mtl-t3-q8_0.gguf chatterbox-mtl-codec-q8_0.gguf --local-dir Chatterbox-Multilingual-TTS

./build/tts-cli synthesize --backbone Chatterbox-Multilingual-TTS/chatterbox-mtl-t3-q8_0.gguf --model Chatterbox-Multilingual-TTS/chatterbox-mtl-codec-q8_0.gguf \
    --text "[en]hello, this is chatterbox speaking." --output out.wav
```

Clone a voice from a few seconds of clean speech (it works across languages):

```bash
./build/tts-cli synthesize ... --ref-audio my_voice.wav --text "[en]hello there." --output out.wav
```

All `tts-cli` options (voices, voice cloning, sampling, GPU) are described in the [codec.cpp README](https://github.com/mybigday/codec.cpp#text-to-speech).


## Python

The `codec_cpp` package runs the same pipeline (it builds codec.cpp with its
bundled llama.cpp, so it needs CMake and a C++ compiler):

```bash
pip install "codec-cpp @ git+https://github.com/mybigday/codec.cpp" huggingface_hub soundfile
```

```python
import codec_cpp, soundfile
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

tts = codec_cpp.TTS(hf_hub_download("BricksDisplay/Chatterbox-Multilingual-TTS-GGUF", "chatterbox-mtl-t3-q8_0.gguf"),
                    hf_hub_download("BricksDisplay/Chatterbox-Multilingual-TTS-GGUF", "chatterbox-mtl-codec-q8_0.gguf"))
audio, sr = tts.synthesize("[en]hello, this is chatterbox speaking.")
soundfile.write("out.wav", audio, sr)
```

`tts.voices()` lists the builtin voices; `ref_audio=` clones a voice where the
model supports it; `tts.stream(text)` yields audio as it is generated. More in
the [Python docs](https://github.com/mybigday/codec.cpp/tree/main/python).


## React Native (llama.rn)

[llama.rn](https://github.com/mybigday/llama.rn) loads the same two files on iOS and Android:

```ts
const ctx = await initLlama({ model: 'chatterbox-mtl-t3-q8_0.gguf', embedding: true })
await ctx.initVocoder({ path: 'chatterbox-mtl-codec-q8_0.gguf' })
const { prompt, grammar, embedding, flow } = await ctx.getFormattedAudioCompletion({
  prompt: 'Hello world',
})
const result = await ctx.completion({ prompt, grammar, embedding })
const pcm = flow === 'continuous_embd'
  ? await ctx.decodeAudioEmbeddings(result.embeddings, result.embedding_dim)
  : await ctx.decodeAudioTokens(result.audio_tokens)
```

Voice cloning, saved voices and per-model notes: [llama.rn TTS docs](https://github.com/mybigday/llama.rn#text-to-speech-tts).


## Input text

Prepare the text as upstream `MTLTokenizer` does:

1. lowercase it and apply Unicode **NFKD** normalization,
2. for Japanese, convert to hiragana; for Chinese, convert to Cangjie codes
   (plain Chinese characters are not pronounced correctly),
3. prefix the language tag: `[en]`, `[fr]`, `[de]`, `[es]`, `[ja]`, `[zh]`, …

```python
import unicodedata
text = "[es]" + unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", "Hola, ¿cómo estás hoy?".lower())
```

Skipping NFKD makes accented letters (é, ó, ü, …) come out wrong.

## Voices

- Builtin voice: `default`.
- Voice cloning: `--ref-audio` with any short, clean clip. Save it with
  `--save-speaker` to reuse it without the clip.

# TangYuGe GPT-SoVITS v2Pro（唐语歌语音合成模型）

**English summary.** A Chinese text-to-speech model of the character *Tang Yuge (唐语歌)* from the visual novel *Sparkling Memories (夏日花火)*, fine-tuned from the official [GPT-SoVITS](https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS) **v2Pro** base models. This repository is self-contained: it ships the fine-tuned GPT and SoVITS weights, all pretrained models required by GPT-SoVITS at inference time, 19 scene reference clips with their prompt texts, ready-to-use profiles and scripts. Chinese only. A newer version fine-tuned from v2ProPlus with noticeably less background noise is available at [shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus](https://huggingface.co/shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus).

本仓库是基于 GPT-SoVITS **v2Pro** 底模微调的唐语歌（《夏日花火》角色）中文语音合成模型，并附带推理所需的全部预训练模型。下载本仓库、准备好 GPT-SoVITS 运行环境后即可直接使用。

> **推荐使用新版本**：[shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus](https://huggingface.co/shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus) 在相同训练数据上改用 v2ProPlus 底模，停顿处底噪低约 5–6 dB、电音更少，发音准确率与声纹相似度持平。本仓库保留用于对比和兼容旧的调用方式。

## 模型信息

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 模型类型 | GPT-SoVITS 少样本语音克隆 / 文本转语音（TTS） |
| 底模 | GPT-SoVITS v2Pro（`s2Gv2Pro.pth`、`s2Dv2Pro.pth`）与 GPT 底模 `s1v3.ckpt` |
| 微调方式 | 全参数微调（非 LoRA），SoVITS 与 GPT 两个模型分别训练 |
| 语言 | 中文（普通话） |
| 输出 | 32 kHz 单声道 WAV |
| 训练数据 | 角色唐语歌的游戏语音 561 条，约 43 分钟 |
| 推荐采样参数 | 多数场景 `top_k=12`、`top_p=0.95`、`temperature=0.9`；以各 profile 中的值为准；切句方式 `cut5` |
| 验证环境 | GPT-SoVITS 提交 `ea2d2a8`、Python 3.10、PyTorch 2.4.0 + CUDA 12.4、NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop 8GB |

## 适用范围

- 适合：为唐语歌这一角色生成中文台词语音，例如同人创作、游戏 Mod、角色对话机器人、个人学习研究。
- 不适合：非中文文本；需要与原声完全一致的商业配音；任何冒充真实人物、误导他人或违法的用途。生成内容请标注为 AI 合成。

## 快速开始

### 1. 准备 GPT-SoVITS

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS.git
cd GPT-SoVITS
git checkout ea2d2a8
```

按 GPT-SoVITS 官方说明安装 Python 依赖（Python 3.10，推荐 NVIDIA GPU）。本仓库已附带所需预训练模型，不需要再单独下载 GPT-SoVITS 的预训练模型包。

### 2. 下载本仓库

建议与 `GPT-SoVITS` 放在同一个父目录下：

```bash
cd ..
hf download shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro --local-dir TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro
```

```text
<workspace>/
├── GPT-SoVITS/
└── TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro/
```

### 3. 安装预训练模型

```bash
python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro/scripts/install_pretrained.py --gptsovits-root GPT-SoVITS
```

脚本会校验文件哈希，再把 `GPT-SoVITS-overlay/` 中的模型复制到 GPT-SoVITS 对应位置（已存在且相同的文件会跳过）。

### 4. 生成语音

以下命令均使用 GPT-SoVITS 的 Python 环境执行：

```bash
# 默认使用主 profile（严肃、长句）
python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro/scripts/run_tangyuge_infer.py --text "这里填写要合成的中文文本。" --output output.wav

# 切换场景：换一个 profile
python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro/scripts/run_tangyuge_infer.py --voice-profile TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro/profiles/morning.yaml --text "早上好呀，今天也要加油哦。" --output morning.wav
```

若两个目录不在同一父目录下，追加 `--gptsovits-root <GPT-SoVITS 路径>`。

### 5. 启动 HTTP 服务（可选）

```bash
python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2pro/scripts/start_tangyuge_bridge.py
```

启动后在 `127.0.0.1:9881` 提供 `/tts` 接口（后端 GPT-SoVITS `api_v2` 运行在 `9880`）。服务会根据文本自动选择场景，也可显式指定：

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9881/tts -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"text": "早上好呀，今天也要加油哦。", "profile": "morning"}' --output output.wav
```

请求字段：`text`（必填）、`profile` / `scene` / `reference`（选择场景）、`top_k`、`top_p`、`temperature` 等。辅助接口：`GET /health`、`GET /profiles`、`GET /references`。

### 在 GPT-SoVITS WebUI 中使用

安装预训练模型后，在 WebUI 推理页选择：

- GPT 模型：`weights/tangyuge_v2pro-e2.ckpt`
- SoVITS 模型：`weights/tangyuge_v2pro_e2_s562.pth`
- 参考音频：`references/` 中任一文件，**参考文本必须使用 `manifests/references.yaml` 中与之绑定的 `prompt_text`**
- 采样参数：`top_k=12`、`top_p=0.95`、`temperature=0.9`

## 场景参考音频（reference）

GPT-SoVITS 的语气和节奏很大程度上由参考音频决定。本仓库提供 19 个场景，每个场景是一条原游戏语音及其台词文本，打包为 `profiles/*.yaml`：

| Profile | 适用文本 |
| --- | --- |
| `main_hybrid_mid`（默认） | 严肃说明、长台词、情绪稳定的表达 |
| `morning` | 早安、问候、短句寒暄 |
| `neutral_polite` | 普通说明、礼貌回答 |
| `soft_daily` | 温柔、日常、低压交流 |
| `question_clear` / `question_firm` | 关切式疑问 / 质询式疑问 |
| `lively_daily` / `casual_invite` | 轻快短句 / 熟人邀请 |
| `narration_calm` | 旁白、叙述 |
| `apology` | 道歉、礼貌退让 |
| `bright_fireworks` / `high_brightness_exclaim` / `exclaim` | 明亮期待 / 开心短句 / 惊讶感叹 |
| `intimate_reassure` / `romantic_soft` | 亲密安抚 / 含蓄恋爱向 |
| `command_gentle` | 提醒、劝阻 |
| `food_daily` / `cafeteria_ordering` | 饮食日常 / 点单 |
| `low_energy_discussion` | 克制解释、舒缓讨论 |

更换参考音频时必须同时更换对应的参考文本，否则发音与节奏会明显变差。

## 训练细节

- 数据：从游戏中提取的唐语歌语音 702 条（约 48.8 分钟），筛选 1–12 秒、有效汉字不少于 6 个的 561 条（约 43.1 分钟）。
- SoVITS：batch size 2，学习率 1e-4，fp16 混合精度，共训练 3 个 epoch，选用第 2 个 epoch（562 步）。
- GPT：batch size 2，16-bit 混合精度，学习率沿用 GPT-SoVITS 默认微调配置，共训练 3 个 epoch，选用第 2 个 epoch。
- 选型：第 1 个 epoch 声纹相似度略高但稳定性较差，第 3 个 epoch 指标下降；人工试听确认第 2 个 epoch 最稳定。详见 `manifests/training_e2_record.md`。

## 评测

- 6 句固定测试文本的声纹相似度（ERes2NetV2，对训练语音平均声纹）为 0.825；原声自身的相似度中位数为 0.914。
- 与新版 v2ProPlus 模型在相同条件下对比：本模型停顿处底噪高约 5–6 dB，DNSMOS 背景噪声分低约 0.2；发音准确率（ASR 拼音错误率约 1–2%）与声纹相似度无显著差异。

## 局限性

- 仅支持中文；中英混合文本效果未验证。
- 部分听众反馈存在一定底噪与电音，新版 v2ProPlus 模型已改善。
- 极短的句子偶尔会只读出前半句，这是 GPT-SoVITS 自回归生成的共性问题。
- 效果依赖参考音频与参考文本的配对；参考文本写错会导致发音、节奏异常。
- 在 CPU 上推理时，部分 Intel 混合架构处理器（已在 i7-13650HX 上复现）的 PyTorch oneDNN 多线程卷积会算出错误结果；GPU 推理不受影响。CPU 推理请设置 `torch.backends.mkldnn.enabled = False` 或使用单线程。
